headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults make Cursor↔Gemini CLI prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads/writes workspace files and clipboard, and Gemini CLI shares state via filesystem and git. That creates a default bridge where one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content. No provenance or isolation is documented, so injection is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF Cursor writes instructions or summaries into shared workspace files that Gemini CLI later reads
IF Gemini CLI treats repository text as actionable instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate worktrees or directories for each agent
Disable clipboard-based handoff between agents
Require a human review step before Gemini CLI consumes Cursor-generated files
Prefix agent-generated artifacts with non-executable markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging or content filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and files in the working directory, and both have broad network egress to external model APIs. Shared filesystem access means sensitive local files can flow into either agent’s context and then out to third-party inference backends by default.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent uploads file contents or context to its model backend during normal operation
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Run each agent in a separate OS user account
Use a redacted copy of the repo for one agent
Turn off or restrict network access for tasks involving sensitive files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses. Cursor explicitly shares state via the local filesystem, while Gemini CLI shares via filesystem and git only. Concurrent edits to the same repo can overwrite each other or corrupt git state in default use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository at the same time
IF either agent commits, rebases, or rewrites files without external locking
mitigations: Assign non-overlapping file ownership per agent
Pause one agent before the other edits the same branch
Use separate branches and merge manually
Run git status before every write step
requires-engineering: add locking around shared repo mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate multi-step outputs and Gemini CLI can act on tool outputs in the terminal. Because both can read/write the same files, one agent’s output can become the other’s input without a verification gate, enabling mistaken facts or bad code to cascade into actions or commits.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI consumes Cursor-produced files or summaries as authoritative
IF either agent uses the other’s output to trigger shell or git actions
mitigations: Require explicit human approval before acting on peer-generated output
Insert a verification checklist before commits or shell execution
Keep generated plans in separate review-only files
Compare outputs against source files before execution
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles clipboard contents and workspace files, while Gemini CLI handles repo files and user-provided directories. If regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches through different cloud backends and logging paths. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI, EU PII, or secrets is stored in the shared workspace
IF either agent’s backend logs or retains that data longer than the other
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared repos
Use synthetic or masked datasets for agent work
Review vendor retention settings before use
Separate compliance-sensitive tasks from general coding tasks
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-handling policy per agent
